text:
Sam Carter: Heads up — audit-scorer flagged a small cluster of admin grants with no owner and last_used > 90d. Also noticed a brief spike in KMS binding events tied to the same service-principals. Thinking a quick triage: snapshot the set, owner outreach, soft-disable (dry-run), then KMS anomaly review. Query I ran:

```sql
SELECT principal, role, last_used, owner
FROM access_admin_grants
WHERE owner IS NULL
  AND last_used < now() - interval '90 days'
ORDER BY last_used ASC
LIMIT 200;
```

Any objections to starting a small canary remediation this afternoon? :eyes:

Maria Chen: No objections. Good catch. Can you add the result CSV to the access-review board and tag me? I'll coordinate owner outreach and the attestation window.

Alex Rivera: Curious about the KMS spike — do you have the raw grant events? If it's the same principals we should check cross-project bindings. Also recommend a dry-run with our scrub tool first:

`rbac-scrub --label orphan-90d --dry-run --output=reports/orphan-90d.csv`

Ida Nguyen: If we proceed, propose this minimal playbook (short):
1) Snapshot ACLs + KMS grants (store in secure bucket).
2) Run `rbac-scrub --dry-run` and review top-20 by risk score.
3) Outreach owners (48h to respond) — if no owner, mark for temporary lock.
4) Auto-deactivate after 7 days (temp lock) unless owner attests.
5) Post-mortem & tagging for policy rule to avoid recurrence.

Also: we should route any KMS-binding anomalies to the KMS team for quick key rotation if a binding looks suspicious.

kms-bot: scan results: 42 principals match orphan-90d label; 7 principals have >3 KMS:Bind events in the last 72h; sample keys: projects/payments/key-rsa-01, projects/ingest/key-ml-02. Full report uploaded to s3://redwood-security-reports/orphan-90d/20260323.csv :white_check_mark:

Sam Carter: Thanks. I'll push the CSV to the access-review board now and start the dry-run. planning to run the dry-run at 16:00 UTC and share diffs in-thread.

sec-oncall: Please @sec-oncall when you post the diffs. I'll join a 20min sync at 16:20 UTC to triage any blocking escalations. If we auto-deactivate anything we'll follow the emergency rollback playbook. :+1:

Alex Rivera: Quick question — for the auto-deactivate step, can we implement a staged window (30m lock -> 24h full disable) so customers/services get a short grace period? Need to avoid surprise incidents.

Ida Nguyen: Yep — staged window makes sense. Add an ephemeral-lock label and an automated rollback hook: if service errors spike >2% in the next 30m we auto-rollback the lock. We'll capture metrics via the rollout tracer.

Maria Chen: I'll prepare the outreach template (short attestation ask + owner contact options) and post in the board. Will also coordinate with SRE on rollback thresholds.

Sam Carter: Running the dry-run now. Will paste the diff snippet when done. Appreciate the quick responses — keeping this canary small (top 20 risk) to avoid blast radius. :lock:

kms-bot: dry-run complete. `rbac-scrub` found 20 high-risk entries in reports/orphan-90d/diff-20260323.json. Sample diff:

```
- principal: svc-ingest-legacy@redwood
- role: project-admin
- last_used: 2023-09-01
+ (would remove: project-admin binding)
```

sec-oncall: Received. Posting a 16:20 UTC invite for a 20m triage. If everyone can join briefly we'll decide on staged locks for the top 5 items. :calendar:

Alex Rivera: I'll be there. If we do the staged lock, I'll wire up the tracer alerts.

Maria Chen: On it — outreach template posted in the board, tagging teams.

Ida Nguyen: I'll draft the rollback runbook snippet and attach it to the ticket.

Sam Carter: Closing loop here after the sync — will post the remediation decisions and the final attestation outcomes in the access-review board. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
